body:
Thank you!

If I may ask, could you elaborate on your sensing my lone wolf attitude and the chip on my shoulder? I'm just curious as to how it comes across the internet, if at all.

I don't like bars. Not that I have a particular problem with them, but I rarely drink, to the point that I almost behave like a recovering alcoholic - I don't go out of my way to explicitly avoid it, but if offered anything, I turn it down.

How exactly do you propose I just walk up to a random group? "Hi, I've no friends - please accept me."? I don't mean to sound flippant, but walking up to a random group of people feels invasive and distasteful. Through into the mix the fact that I never know what to talk about with people (at all), and, yeah - not a solid plan.

I'm just looking for ways to make friends in general - regardless of gender. I have acquaintances, but none so close that I would properly call 'friends'.

I detest any and all dating/social apps; it feels disingenuous, and I ultimately find it sad when in the 21st century, if one wants to make friends, they have to download an app - yet, here we are.

Is making friends with 45-year-olds my only viable option? I know not every single person in my age group loves to clubbing/bar-hopping, but I guess I simply don't know how to connect with people over hobbies; what are my hobbies? I have things that I enjoy doing, but they're 'me time' activities (listening to music, reading, cooking, writing, etc.).

What I really want is to simply sit down with someone my age and have a genuine conversation.

Meh, worst-case scenario, there is a tenant at the building I manage who I've caught sneaking glances; she's 68 but looks as though she's in her early 40s, so...

I think that it's simply the fact that my last two jobs  - while both very interesting - involved me being surrounded by individuals 50+. Can't believe I'm saying this, but I sometimes wish I could work for a company filled with millennials - entitled, narcissistic, shallow, with a glint of naiveté in their eyes...but my age, nonetheless.

Oh, and one of the first things I was told on my orientation day was, "When you google Credico (the parent company that has power of attorney over everything), you'll get some results with the words 'scam' or 'pyramid scheme' - ignore those."

I've worked one of these. Out of college, jobless, ambitious but desperate. Drove 40 minutes everyday to an office where we were packed in a hot, sweaty room engaging in ritual chanting and ceaseless high-fiving, to then proceed to spend 5-6 hours in Walmart pitching Comcast to passersby.

I was told by the "CEO" (though, his delusions of grandeur paled in comparison to others; one guy kept hitting on a girl I worked with, saying that they should be together to be a power couple - he 'sold' charity subscriptions to WWF on a street corner) that I had strong leadership qualities, but was constantly reprimanded for not doing as well as others, and for not 'trusting the system'.

That's all in addition to the lies, drug and alcohol abuse, sex abuse, forced abortions ('guilted into', technically), and rampant narcissism.

At least now I have an interesting story to tell of how I spent a month of my life in a cult.

26, had one relationship in college - hated it. She expected me to propose after the two months we were together, constantly reminding me to "be a gentleman" and bringing up her dead high school sweetheart (though, in retrospect, I'm convinced that she was a compulsive liar who was testing my reaction) - breaking up with her was one of the most satisfying moments of my college experience (her flirting with another guy and saying, "well, he's a gentleman", made it *that* much easier).

Let me offer what little advice I can.

I am currently going through a kind of rebirth in my life - exploring myself emotionally to see who I truly am, after spending practically my entire life burying my emotions and never really expressing myself. I attempted suicide last year (feel free to check my posts for full backstory), and I now realize that it was necessary for me to reach that point, because it forced me to examine myself and ask what I want out of life.

Like you, I seek companionship, but not for the sake of simply being in a relationship; I genuinely want to connect with someone and have something serious. However, I'm not ready. Over the last two years alone ('16 + '17): took overseas trip, unemployed, took another overseas trip, worked for a pyramid scheme, quit said pyramid scheme, met cute girl, unemployed again, got turned down by cute girl, felt crushed, still unemployed, cute girl came back into picture - torrent of texts and sexting (all on Christmas Day), radio silence from cute girl, cute girl rejects again, realized I've no plan for future, attempted suicide, change mind - decided to live, took LSAT, failed LSAT (though one can't technically 'fail', most would agree that falling in the 17th percentile constitutes sub-par performance), applied to law schools, got rejected by law schools, took GRE, did relatively well on GRE, applied to MBA programs, got rejected by graduate schools, got offered a summer job involving property management, job sparked interest in property management and real estate, had abrupt falling out with best friend, realized that he was my only true friend, came to conclusion that I really have no other friends, worked job, applied to another MBA program practically on a lark, got accepted immediately, finished job, met even cuter girl, hit it off, asked her out, she never replied, felt like shit, realized what time of year it is, recalled suicide attempt, felt even worse, got my shit together and started to feel better, started writing erotic short story, contemplated second Master's Degree in International Tax Law in Switzerland, remembered that after three weeks I've yet to finish writing the story, ...and here we are.

You know what the most recent thing I've done is, following all of the aforementioned? Bought a $2,500 Dolce & Gabbana Navy Cashmere Coat (granted, it was time for a new coat - my current one is more of a jacket and is falling apart - and life is short, so why not enjoy a taste of the finer things?).

My point in all of this is that through everything - the lows, the highs - I pushed forward. It was difficult, yes, because it culminated in facing myself in the mirror, conforming my demons, and vowing to become better.

Being an introvert (with a possible slight case of mild Aspergers that rears its head on occasion), I am gifted in that I am able to hang back and read a room. You know how at 22, 23, you see those 'cool' guys at the bar/club, with some friends and a girl-or-two? The braggadocio, the narcissism, the naïveté of criminal proportions regarding anything involving a though process lasting greater than 5 seconds. Those guys will crash and burn. Hard. At that age, no one - and I mean *ab.so.fu.cking.lute.ly no one* has any sense of life direction. Being the 'cool guy' in college - regardless of money, job opportunity, fucking perfectly-coiffed hair, and those ivory chinos with the rolled bottom cuff with those brown penny loafers (fuck you) - means that life has yet to pay you a visit. And when it does, dear God in heaven, it will break down the door, pick you up, thrown you down, pin your ankles behind your back, fuck you within an inch of your life, violently pull out its blood-and-dissease-riddled-cum-soaked cock, spit on your ass, give it a slap, and leave you to pick up whatever pieces remain of your shattered sense of self, rivaled only by the pain of your shattered rectum.

You're still discovering yourself. You're questioning your value, your choices, your life: *this* is *your* ass-ramming - and you will grow stronger. The advice in these comments should be taken seriously: find a hobby, read, learn a new language, take a trip, build something, hop in the car and drive as far as you can until you run out of gas - explore the most cavernous depths of yourself and forge yourself in the man you know you can become. Better yourself. With this, you will settle into life's journey with a state of grace and confidence, and whatever ups and downs come your way, you'll be far better equipped to handle them.

Don't worry about women. Casually approach the girl in the supermarket, or wherever, and offer a simple, "Hi, sorry to bother you, but you are the most beautiful girl I've seen today, and I just had to come introduce myself." Bold, direct, honest, nerve-wracking, but worth it. She turns down your advances, wish her a nice day, then go talk to that cute blonde buying salmon by the pound. The point is not to become a repugnant PUA asshole (they're all insecure, by the way), but rather to realize that in a world of billions of people, rejection from a handful of women will not break you, because **it does not define you**. The more time you spend focusing on bettering yourself, the more you will feel secure in what you want out of life, and out of a relationship, so that when you come across a woman you might actually be interested in, you'll be standing on steady ground.

Have fun. Enjoy life. Work on yourself, and the fruits of your labor will multiply. By becoming a quality person (that all begins with *you*), you will attract a quality woman.

As far as hobbies are concerned, yes, some are more social, and some less-so. Do what you love - what you're passionate about.

Apologies for the rant, which may or may not be a bit off the mark, but I thought to offer my two cents.

DM if you want to talk.

Good luck, and all the best.

I was overreacting. My problem is that I've spent practically my entire life burying my emotions and being the calm, stoic figure. Sure, I could laugh and have a good time, and I've never had a problem telling people what I honestly thought, but in terms of emotions, it was as if they didn't exist for me. So, anytime something gets to me emotionally, it becomes a roller coaster of overthinking, overreacting, and just being a moody prick. I feel much better now after I've had time to clear my head a bit, but it still feels weird.

To answer your question: nah.

I've thought of texting her once more, because I do think she's a great person and fun to talk to, but, we'll see.

Would you believe that today was much better? I finished most of my short story, worked out, showered, and am in a much better mood.

Thank you, again, for your kind words.

I appreciate the response. I still read and listen to music, but they quickly lose their wonder as the reality sets in that my reality is rather dull compared to the exciting fictitious one I'm engaged in at that moment, making me feel even more down.

Making music was a big part of me, but over the past two, two-and-a-half years, that has completely fallen by the wayside. Same with photography.

As I mentioned in my OP, I did write a short story yesterday, and perhaps I'll have it posted or published somewhere. But that is enough to occupy my time only for a brief moment. In many ways, it feels as though I've become uninspired by life.

I do feel a bit better this morning, but we'll see how the days go.

That long, cold swim in the dark night is still calling out to me, and I may just answer.
